interest: Shows postwar Japan's Peruvian Nisei association, cautious SCAP handling of a Japanese war-research institute, and bogus claims groups.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.43, Japan: Societies) spans August 1946 to March 1948 and consists of correspondence, diplomatic despatches, charters, and instructions relating to various private, commercial, and research associations operating in or concerned with occupied Japan. The file covers four distinct subjects: congressional and State Department correspondence regarding 'Liberated Military Personnel (Japan)', an unauthorized Washington-based entity soliciting claims from former prisoners of war; the establishment in Tokyo of the Peruvian Nisei Association of Japan (Asociación de Niseis Peruanos del Japón), whose founding statutes were transmitted via U.S. diplomatic channels in Yokohama and Washington to the Peruvian government in Lima; an appeal from Shujiro Iwasaki, president of the Tokyo International Club, to President Harry S. Truman seeking American guidance and commercial ties to foster peaceful trade and spread democracy; and a proposal submitted through the Japanese Central Liaison Office to establish the Peace Construction Research Institute to investigate the historical causes and material losses of Japan's recent wars, which U.S. occupation authorities deemed premature prior to a formal peace treaty.

subfiles.from: Peruvian Nisei Association of Japan (Asociación de Niseis Peruanos del Japón)
subfiles.summary: Preceded by an official enclosure cover slip, this document contains the 22 articles comprising the constitution of the Peruvian Nisei Association of Japan. The statutes specify that the organization aims to promote mutual friendship, protect the interests of Peruvian citizens in Japan, and pursue cultural and scientific activities, while permitting participation by individuals from other Latin American nations. Article 7 explicitly prohibits the association from intervening in Japanese domestic or foreign politics, and subsequent chapters establish a Deliberative Commission, annual general assemblies, administrative divisions, and a schedule of monthly dues in yen.

subfiles.about: The formal prospectus, articles of incorporation, program of work, and estimated budget for the proposed Peace Construction Research Institute.
subfiles.from: Organizers of the Peace Construction Research Institute
subfiles.summary: This five-page enclosure sets forth the detailed foundational scheme for the Peace Construction Research Institute as a foundational juridical person based in Shiba-ku, Tokyo. The institute's mandate was to conduct comprehensive interdisciplinary investigations into the causes of the Manchurian Incident, the Sino-Japanese Affair, and the Pacific War, while documenting the loss of life, property destruction, and severe privations suffered by the Japanese population to ensure future peace. The document details the governance structure of directors, superintendents, and a 50-member board of trustees, along with a five-year operational plan (October 1946 to March 1951) and an annual operating budget of 239,650 yen funded primarily by government research commissions.
subfiles.title: Prospectus, Articles of Incorporation, and Budget of the Proposed Peace Construction Research Institute
subfiles.to: Japanese Central Liaison Office / Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
